sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 07.08.2021 at about 12 noon when petitioner was travelling in Auto along with her parents and his father viz. Chikkaraju.H.C. was driving Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-52-9579, on left side of road, on NH-75, Kunigal-Nelamangala Road, Opp.

Bhavani Shanker House, Hanchipura Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time the respondent's Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to Auto.

Due to which, she sustained grievous injuries and thereafter she was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.30,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyances,
nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was aged about 2 years.
Due to the accidental injuries, she suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The respondents being the RC owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed his written statement.

4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has filed counter to petition by denying the petition averments.
He has further disputed the manner of accident, age of injured and quantum of compensation claimed under different heads.

Further contended that according to FIR, the complainant/Chikkaraju driver cum owner of autorickshaw was proceeding along with his wife and child near Bhavani Shankar House Hanchipura Gate, at that time one lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 its driver without any signal taken vehicle right side of road and the driver of autorickshaw not avoided the accident and Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23980599/
2 dashed to the lorry petrol tank and fell down all the persons and sustained grievous injuries.

The driver of lorry has taken all cautions with signal but the driver of Auto was without observing indication and high speedy running his vehicle and selflessly dashed to lorry and sustained injuries.

Further contended that the auto rickshaw cab driver cum owner was having the permit to Nelamangala Rural Area and but alleged accident occurred out of permit area and also the owner of autorickshaw cab using the vehicle on NH-75 Road, according to permit running on NH Road is prohibited.
Hence, violated permit conditions.

Further contended that the auto rickshaw cab driver cum owner was holding DL to non transport and the M.V. No.KA-52-9579 Autorickshaw Cab/Passenger vehicle is transport vehicle, but he was not holding the badge at the time of accident .

Further contended that 1 st respondent is insured with this respondent under policy No.171001/31/20/P114635690 valid from 18.03.2021 to 17.03.2022 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following :
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.08.2021 at about 12 noon, on NH-75, Kunigal-Nelamangala Road,
Opp Bhavani Shankar House, Hanchipura Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District, while she was proceeding in a Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-52- 9579, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove her case, the Guardian/father of petitioner has examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his side of evidence.

The RTO of Regional Transport Commissioner, Nelamangala deputed one Sri.Vijaykumar.C, Superintendent and he has been examined as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & Ex.R.2 and closed his side of evidence.
7. I have heard arguments on the side of petitioner and respondent No.2 perused the materials available on records.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed written arguments.
I have carefully perused the written arguments filed by learned counsel for respondent No.2.

Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23980599/
3 8.
It is the case of petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry, the accident occurred.
The guardian of petitioner alleged that the driver of lorry all of a sudden took towards right side, as a result the accident occurred.
Father of petitioner gave statement as per EXP2 before police in hospital by alleging that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
On the basis of Ex.P.2, police have registered the case as per Ex.P.1 and thereafter the police went near the place of accident and drew up mahazar as per Ex.P.4 by narrating the place of accident.
As per mahazar, the accident occurred on National Highway in between auto and lorry.
PW.1 in his chief examination he has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry the accident occurred.
Even in his cross examination he has deposed that due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry the accident occurred.
On meticulous perusal of evidence of PW.1, the respondent insurance company nothing elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

The police after thorough investigation prepared sketch and after completion of investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending lorry for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
10.
The learned counsel for respondent insurance company filed written arguments.

In his written arguments he has submitted that the Air Cab belongs to petitioners holding the permit to Nelamangala radius only i.e., 5 Kms, but the petitioner violated the conditions of permit, he was going to Tumkur District Hebbur i.e., 50 Kms, but authority issued permit only rural area of 5 Kms and he was running in National Highway.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have filed charge sheet only against the lorry.

Further the learned counsel for respondent insurance company submitted that RW.1 i.e., RTO Nelamangala Superintendent examined and produced permit extract and marked as exhibit and as per permit only permitted in rural limits of Nelamangala.
The accident occurred on National Highway and not on service road, as such petitioner violated the permit conditions.
11. In order to prove the contention of respondent insurance company, he has summoned Superintendent, RTO, Nelamangala.
He has deposed in his chief examination that he has produced Ex.R.2 permit.
Further he has deposed that as per permit, the auto can ply within the radius of 5 Kms from Nelamangala and it is not permitted on National Highway, but it can be ply on service road.
PW.1 in his cross examination, he has deposed that he was going from Hebbur to Nelamangala and he himself was driving the auto.
Further he has deposed that the permit was given within the radius of 5 Kms of Nelamangala Rural.

Further in his cross examination, he has deposed that he has Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23980599/
4 seen the lorry which was parked 20 feet away from him, the lorry all of a sudden took towards right side as a result there was an accident.
After investigation police filed charge sheet against the driver of offending Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922.
In charge sheet it is alleged that the driver of lorry without observing the vehicle negligently took his lorry towards right side as a result the accident occurred.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 - Sketch, the accident occurred on National Highway in the middle of road.
Even in IMV Report mentioned the damages to auto and lorry.
As per Ex.P.8 - IMV Report, Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB- 3922 right side rear wheel mudguard and fuel tank right side damaged.
On meticulous perusal of Ex.P.8 IMV Report it corroborates case of petitioner.
The I.O has not alleged that there was a negligence on the part of petitioner, it clearly alleged that due to negligence on the part of offending lorry the accident occurred.
Now the contention of respondent insurance that the auto violated the permit conditions.
As per I.O. and case of petitioner the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company nothing placed before the tribunal to show that only due to negligence on the part of petitioner the accident occurred.
Only on the basis of violation of permit the respondent cannot escape from his liability, because the accident occurred due to whole negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company has not placed any materials before the tribunal to show that the insured lorry violated terms and conditions of policy.
So, under such circumstances the respondent insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

On perusal of all the police and hospital documents placed by the petitioner, it is evident that there was a road traffic accident and in the said accident petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.9, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the affirmative, the minor petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.
13.
The Father/Guardian of minor petitioner contended that due to accident his daughter sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries caused to her, the father of petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by Nelamangala Taluk Hospital at Ex.P.3.
On perusal of Ex.P.3, the petitioner Dhanyantha Gowda sustained head injury and abrasions injuries and doctor has opined that injuries are simple in nature.

In order to prove the injuries sustained by the petitioner,
petitioner has not examined doctor to prove her disability.
The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show that they have paid medical expenses to the hospital.
So, under such circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for medical expenses.
On perusal of the wound certificate produced by the petitioner, the minor petitioner sustained simple injuries.

By considering facts and circumstances, the minor petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.30,000/-.
14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23980599/
5 No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka at Page Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver.
The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs. 30,000/- (Rupees Thirty thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

The entire compensation amount shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank nearer to her place for three years or till she attains age of majority whichever is later without encumbrance.
The father/Natural Guardian of petitioner is entitled for interest that accrues on FD periodically.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested Dhanyatha Gowda.C vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23980599/
6 by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to her account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Office to draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 16th day of February, 2023.)
(D.RAGHAVENDRA)
